tossups.text: A fourth symphony from this country features a 4/2 C-major fugue and often requires two conductors. A pianist from this country wrote Bamboula and Le Bananier["bah-nah-nee-ay"], while a set of Woodland Sketches from this country includes "To a Wild Rose." A solo trumpet phrase repeated seven times poses an "Unanswered Question" in a work from this country. A composer from this country consulted the I Ching for his Music of Changes and wrote Sonatas and Interludes for prepared piano. For 10 points, name this country where a piece consisting of 4 minutes and 33 seconds of silence was written, the home of Charles Ives and John Cage.

In this work, hunters and their Berkshire hounds cause the speaker to flee and notice an omen backed by the sunset that calls up memories from the Arno-vale. Its speaker strays to the hills, where he notices "twisted chimney-stacks" and sees the "tender purple spray" on the copse and briers. The speaker laments the loss of his shepherd's pipes and remembers his companion's "rustic flute," which too quickly gained a "stormy note." The end of this poem sees the title character whisper to the speaker that "The light we sought is shining still," despite the fact that he "wander'd til died." Exalting Oxford as "that sweet city with her dreaming spires," this poem uses the image of a "signal-elm" tree to represent the friendship between the title character and the speaker, Corydon. Styled after Virgil's Seventh Eclogue, for 10 points, name this Matthew Arnold elegy to Arthur Hugh Clough.

A book titled for this phrase contains an analysis of "stable intermediate forms" inspired by a Herbert Simon argument about two watchmakers, and introduces the concept of something that is both a whole and a part, which this book terms a "holon." That book with this title argues that the pre-human features of the brain are responsible for emotions and destructive impulses, and was written by Arthur Koestler. This phrase was coined to be "deliberately abusive" in an earlier book that argues against a longstanding "category mistake," which the book also refers to as "the official doctrine" in the section "Descartes' Myth." For 10 points, give this phrase used in The Concept of Mind by Gilbert Ryle to denounce mind-body dualism.

Evidence of an advanced writing system for this civilization was found on a Dholavira signboard containing 26 symbols. The Priest King and Dancing Girl statues were found in one city of this civilization, another of which was the port of Lothal. That city included the "College of Priests" and the "Great Bath." An Aryan invasion is a theoretical cause for the destruction of this civilization that included the cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro. For 10 points, name this Bronze Age civilization centered around a namesake south Asian river.

This poem's speaker feels a "fierce fire [crawling] about a thousand people" and hears "a thousand screams" when two ships sink after crashing at sea. That speaker is subjected to a power that shows her the "gossiping of friendly spheres" and "[t]he How and Why of all things," making her feel like a "fearful pawn." This poem caused a scandal after losing to an Orrick Johns work in a poetry contest held by The Lyric Year.Twice, this poem describes a "drenched and dripping apple-tree," soaked by a rain that "wash[es] my grave away from me." The speaker of this poem, which was written from Mt. Battie in Camden, Maine, tries to touch the sky as Infinity descends on her. This poem's speaker imagines being buried in the ground and then being raised back out of it, and concludes that "he whose soul is flat-the sky will cave in on him by and by." For 10 points, name this poem by Edna St. Vincent Millay that begins, "All I could see from where I stood was three long mountains and a wood."

Gottfried Leibniz wrote a chapter-by-chapter rebuttal to one of this thinker's works. This man proposed that humans are born without innate ideas, and that the mind is a "tabula rasa" or "blank slate" in his Essay Concerning Human Understanding. For 10 points, name this English philosopher who wrote Two Treatises of Government in which he cited life, liberty, and property as things the government must protect.

A version of this technique separates samples by their isoelectric point and can be performed in its two-dimensional variant. Capillary action moves the results of this technique onto a nitrocellulose membrane in a Southern Blot. The amphipathic nature of sodium dodecyl sulfate allows it to separate both polar and nonpolar sections during the preparation for one variant for this technique, after which it is placed in polyacrylamide [PAUL-lee-uh-KRILL-uh-MIDE]. Samples in this technique are most often placed in the polysaccharide agarose, which contains wells for the samples near the anode. For ten points, name this technique which uses electricity to separate DNA fragments by size.
acceptableAnswers: sodium dodecyl sulfate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis

tossups.text: A common demonstration of this phenomenon uses it to measure the width of a strand of hair. Fraunhofer and Fresnel ("fruh-NELL") name the far-field and near-field types of this phenomenon, respectively. The most common application of Huygens ("HOY-gens") principle is used to model this phenomenon. The equation "2 d sine theta equals n times lambda" describes this phenomenon. Electrons underwent this phenomenon after being fired at a nickel target in the Davisson-Germer experiment. This phenomenon is described by Bragg's law. A series of thin slits make up this phenomenon's namesake grating. For 10 points, name this phenomenon where light bends around an obstacle.

The number one is subtracted from this quantity in the formula for a system's Damkohler number. The overall amount for this quantity is calculated by finding the partial amounts for it in the Ostwald isolation method. This quantity and initial concentration must be the same for all processes in a system so that Wegscheider's principle applies. The units of the pre-exponential factor A depend on this quantity; for example, A has units inverse-seconds when this quantity is equal to one. An easy way to determine this quantity is to find the slope of the natural log of rate with respect to the natural log of a reactant's concentration. For chain and radical reactions, this quantity, which is frequently mistaken for molecularity, is often fractional, and when it is equal to two, a simplifying assumption where this quantity is "pseudo first" is often employed. For 10 points, identify this quantity, which for a substance in a chemical reaction corresponds to the exponent to which that substance's concentration is raised in the rate law.

Richard Porson worked on reconstructing parts of the lower right portion of this object, which was recovered from the walls of Fort Julien. It served as the basis for most of the work contained in the Letter to Monsieur Dacier, which expanded on earlier work done using this object by Thomas Young. This object, long also known as EA 24, was first rediscovered by Pierre-François Bouchard. It names Aëtus son of Aëtus as the priest of the cult of Alexander the Great and describes how the gods have awarded victory, strength, and "life, prosperity, and health", the latter trio represented as "ankh wedja seneb", to Ptolemy V. For 10 points, name this object used by Jean-Francois Champollion to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphics.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for gut microbiome. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this colon-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The colon is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in gut microbiome.

tossups.text: According to Herodotus, this empire's founder had his head dunked in a jar of blood by the queen of the Massagetae, Tomyris. This empire crushed the armies of Nabonidus at the Battle of Opis. This empire was ruled by provincial satraps, who answered to "Kings of Kings" like Cambyses II and Darius I. This empire's first invasion of Greece was defeated at the Battle of Marathon. For 10 points, name this empire ruled by the Achaemenid dynasty of Cyrus the Great
acceptableAnswers: the Achaemenid Empire until it is read
the Achaemenian Dynasty until it is read

tossups.text: In geometries named for this figure, there are multiple lines parallel to a given line through a given noncollinear point. The orbit of unbound comets takes this shape, and the three-dimensional analogues of this conic section can be of one or two sheets. Formally defined as the locus of points the difference of whose distances to two foci (FOH-sai) is a constant and exemplified by the graph of y equals one over x, name this conic section with a eccentricity greater than one and two separate branches.

In this novel, one character plans to tie a young girl to a loom to keep her from wandering off. Two characters in this novel are confused by the letters "I.H.S." appearing on lard cakes, and one of them had earlier falsely accused Jem Rodney of a crime, though the real perpetrator's skeleton is later found in a ditch. Molly Farren's death clears the way for Nancy Lammeter's marriage in this novel, which focuses on a character who leaves Lantern Yard due to the efforts of William Dane. After the theft of his gold by Dunstan, the title character of this novel adopts the daughter of Godfrey Cass, Eppie. For 10 points, name this novel about the title weaver of Raveloe, a work by George Eliot.

The Pound-Rebka-Snider experiment confirmed the Einstein or gravitational version of this effect, which also occurs when two beamed energy sources interact, an interaction known as the Wolf Effect. The Relativistic Doppler effect provides an exact equation for calculating this, an approximate form of which is z = v divided by c, where v is the velocity of the source of light that is moving away from the viewer. For 10 points, name this effect used as evidence the universe is expanding and to calculate the distance of distant galaxies, an apparent lengthening of the wavelength of light from its source to its observation.

Instructions for making a Mobius strip precede a collection by this man whose title story centers on a trip to the boardwalk on July Fourth with Magda. Another of his books features a parody of Ernst Haeckel named Max Spielman, who coins such phrases as "proctoscopy repeats hagiography." That novel by this man sees Billy Bocksfuss complete all the stages of Joseph Campbell's monomyth on the way to entering WESCAC and becoming the Grand Tutor of New Tammany College. This author of Lost in the Funhouse was inspired by a colonial poem to write a novel in which Henry Burlingame III tutors Ebenezer Cooke, whose title evokes an antiquated term for tobacco. For 10 points, name this Maryland-born author of Giles Goat-Boy and The Sot-Weed Factor.

It's not FDR, but this person attacked a 2 million dollar yacht in a speech claiming, "There's no such thing as left or right, only up or down" and describing a "rendezvous with destiny." Another speech by this person said he had not "seen the last" of a group that "slipped the surly bonds of earth to touch the face of God." This man gave a speech supporting the Republican candidate in the election of 1964, Barry Goldwater, entitled "A Time for Choosing." This man also urged another world leader, "[I]f you seek liberalization, come here to this gate," and then shouted, "[T]ear down this wall!" For 10 points, name this U.S. president who defeated Jimmy Carter in the election of 1980.

During a historical period with this number in its name, a major figure would wander the countryside offering his expertise in siegecraft to imperiled cities if they allowed him to tell them about universal love. Lian Qichao and Kang Youwei led a reform identified by this number under Guangxu that ended with an 1898 coup by Cixi. The speech "On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People" ended a "campaign" defined by this number, which briefly allowed anti-state criticism. Mao's abortive reform was named for this many flowers, equal to the number of days between Napoleon's escape from Elba and defeat at Waterloo. For 10 points, give this number of years identifying a medieval war between France and England actually lasting from 1337 to 1453.

This region, known by ancient denizens as the "Mining Country," may have received its modern name from a god who rode a winged bull and had a beard made of lapis lazuli. Pompey was murdered in one city in this region while a waterway built by Necho was later converted into "Trajan's River." In modern history, this region was the target of of Operation Badr to seize the Bar Lev Line, occurring simultaneously with an other Islamic nation's attempt to conquer the Golan Heights during the Yom Kippur War. Anwar Sadat allowed another nation to traverse this peninsula navally through a canal after signing its namesake "Disengagement Act."For 10 points, name this peninsula that acts as a land bridge between Africa and Asia in the nation of Egypt.

Hyaluronic acid is the only GAG that does not contain this element. Two oxygens are double-bonded to this element in a functional group used to make alcohols undergo SN2 reactions, called a tosyl group. The rigid structure of keratin is due to the presence of stabilizing bonds between two atoms of this element. This element is replaced with selenium in analogues of the amino acids methionine and cysteine, which form "bridges" with this element. This element is added to create cross-linking in rubber in vulcanization, and its most common allotrope is an eight-atom ring. For 10 points, what element combines with hydrogen to form a gas that smells like rotten eggs?

parts.text: The duckwalk and death drops are common elements of this dance style, which rose to prominence following the release of the documentary Paris is Burning. Dancers strike poses to emulate runway models in this dance style.

The angular arms and rigid poses of figures in this ancient Egyptian writing system also inspired elements of vogue, specifically hand performance and arm control. This writing system is found on the Rosetta Stone.
This American singer popularized vogue in the music video for her song of the same name. Other songs by this singer include "Like a Virgin" and "Like a Prayer."

bonuses.leadin: This house dance style originated in black and Latino LGBT communities in Harlem in the 1970s. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this language of many works featuring King Bahram, including the epic Shahnameh.

The "Three Princes of Serendip" tale was originally added to a long poem by this author in which Bahram houses his seven brides in seven planet-themed palaces. That poem is part of his Khamsa, along with the tale of Layla and Majnun.

A poem credited to this author describes how the wild ass stamps over the head of King Bahram, but "cannot break his sleep." This poet wrote of a "Moving Finger that writes; and, having writ, moves on."
acceptableAnswers: prompt on Edward Fitzgerald by asking “whose work was he translating?”

bonuses.leadin: A story originally from this language, in which three princes from Serendip explain to King Bahram how they deduced the appearance of a lost camel, inspired Horace Walpole to coin the term "serendipity." For 10 points each:

parts.text: The most important fasting time is this 40-day period stretching from Clean Monday till the vigil on Easter churches. In Western Christianity, this period begins on Ash Wednesday.
A two-week fast precedes this Orthodox holiday, which commemorates the death of the Theotokos. An Epitaphios of Mary is paraded on this holiday.

Besides Lent and the Dormition, the other two main fasts are the Nativity Fast, and this fast, which honors the fast that the title group observed for the ten days after Christ's Ascension, in preparation for receiving the Holy Spirit.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about periods of fasting in the Eastern Orthodox Church, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this Revolutionary War traitor who intended to surrender West Point to the British in exchange for 20,000 pounds.
Arnold led the capture of Fort Ticonderoga with this Vermonter and leader of the Green Mountain Boys.
After the capture of Fort Ticonderoga, Henry Knox led a team that hauled sixty tons of heavy artillery across New York and Massachusetts to this city, Massachusetts's largest city.

bonuses.leadin: This man was one of the leaders of the capture of Fort Ticonderoga, and he married Peggy Shippen, a Loyalist and close friend of British military leader John André. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name both of these warring genres of comedy prevalent in 18th-century England. One showed virtue triumphing over vice, but didn't emphasize humor; the other, descended from comedy of manners, aimed mainly to be funny.
Goldsmith himself wrote this shining example of laughing comedy, in which Tony Lumpkin tricks Charles Marlow into thinking that the Hardcastle estate is an inn.
The pioneering sentimental comedy was Love's Last Shift by this one-time Poet Laureate. This playwright replaced Lewis Theobald as King of Dunces in the 1743 edition of Pope's The Dunciad.

bonuses.leadin: Oliver Goldsmith championed one of these two genres in an essay titled A Comparison between these two genres. The other genre was championed by Beaumarchais ("bo-mar-SHAY"), among others. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man whose translation of those plates became the major text of the religion he founded.
Joseph Smith founded this religion, whose well-known followers include Steve Young and Mitt Romney.
More than half of this western state's population identifies as Mormon. This state contains Brigham Young University.

bonuses.leadin: The angel Moroni told this man the location of the golden plates, which were outside of his western New York home. For 10 points:

parts.text: That aforementioned description is a simplified model of what interacting groups of two electrons, whose contribution to a system only becomes sufficiently large when thermal motion is low?
Cooper pairs are predicted by BCS theory, which describes this phenomenon, in which a substance has developed a near-zero value for resistance.
Superconductivity is exploited to create these very precise magnetometers, in which the magnetic flux is measured at a Josephson junction.

bonuses.leadin: A simple qualitative picture of them is that a free electron exerts attractive forces on positive ions, which in turn exerts an attractive force on another free electron, bounding the two. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this process in which biological functions like breathing and brain activity end.
One easy way to realize you have died is if you experience this condition in which your limbs become stiff since muscle tissues are unable to relax.
Decomposition of the body following death leads to this sign as anaerobic metabolism from bacteria inside the body results in gases accumulating inside the body.

bonuses.leadin: 100% of people who go through this process do not live to tell the tale. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these roughly spherical components of dark matter that surround the visible portion of galaxies. These components were hypothesized when Vera Rubin discovered the non-Keplerian nature of rotation curves.
Halos prominently emit light in this portion of the spectrum with wavelengths between those of ultraviolet and gamma radiation.
This doubly eponymous model for hierarchical structure formation was derived by modeling the distribution of halo mass as a Gaussian random field.

bonuses.leadin: MACHOs exist in these building blocks for structure formation. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this member of the First Triumvirate who later fought a civil war against his fellow triumvir Caesar.
Pompey was assassinated in Egypt after losing this decisive battle of 48 BC, later commemorated in an epic poem by Lucan.
For his campaign against the pirates Pompey was given proconsular powers over the Mediterranean and coastal regions up to 50 miles inland by this law, named for the tribune who proposed it.

bonuses.leadin: He finished off the Third Mithridatic War and cleared the supporters of Marius from the isle of Sicily on behalf of Sulla. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with layers of the heart wall.
What is the main function of the atrium in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to layers of the heart wall.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this 1605 attempt to assassinate King James I and replace England's Protestant government with a Catholic one. It failed when its namesake explosive substance was discovered and confiscated.
British citizens remember the Gunpowder Plot by celebrating Bonfire Night on the fifth of November, in which effigies of this man, who is traditionally depicted with a smiling mask, are burned.
Robert Catesby and Guy Fawkes attempted to overthrow King James I by blowing up this building, which is home to the House of Lords and the House of Commons.

bonuses.leadin: Participants in this event included Thomas Winter, Thomas Percy, and their leader, Robert Catesby. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Identify this resistive force, whose varieties include sliding, rolling, kinetic, and static.
Friction is related to this other force by the coefficient of friction. It is defined as the contact force perpendicular to the surface.
This law states that kinetic friction is independent of sliding velocity. This law's namesake is also the namesake of the unit of electric charge.

bonuses.leadin: Air resistance is a form of this. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this profession shared by Feste, Trinculo and a character whose final appearance has him say "And I'll go to bed at Noon" before disappearing for the rest of the play.
The fool who disappears in this play is thought to have been double cast with Cordelia. In this Shakespeare play, the kingdom of the title monarch is split among his daughters

Touchstone falls in love with the shepherdess Audrey in this other Shakespeare play, whose first act centers around a wrestling match. In this play, Touchstone threatens to kill anyone "a hundred and fifty ways" if they attempt to marry Audrey.

bonuses.leadin: One character of this profession notes "Many a good hanging prevents a bad marriage." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these 24-hour biological cycles that include sleeping and waking. They are regulated by signals called entrainers.
Circadian rhythms are partly controlled by the release of melatonin from this small gland in the brain. Hagfish notably lack them.
This nucleus, located in the anterior hypothalamus, is the master regulator of circadian rhythms. It's named for its position right above the crossing of the optic nerves.

bonuses.leadin: The per and cry genes help mediate these processes in humans. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this poet whose first collection was entitled Just Give Me a Cool Drink of Water 'fore I Diiie.
Angelou is best known for this autobiography, which takes its title from a Paul Laurence Dunbar poem. It describes Angelou's upbringing in Stamps, Arkansas.
parts.answer: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
acceptableAnswers: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
The I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings

parts.text: Angelou wrote and read her poem "On the Pulse of Morning" for one of these events. Other poetry readings at these events have included Richard Blanco's "One Today" and Robert Frost's "The Gift Outright."

bonuses.leadin: Sections like "Touch Me, Life, Not Softly" appear in this poet's collection And Still I Rise. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This 1571 victory for Don John of Austria's majority-Spanish Holy League over Ali Pasha near Greece demolished Ottoman naval power in the Mediterranean.
A pre-Trafalgar victory for Horatio Nelson, this August 1798 defeat for Napoleon was technically fought in Aboukir Bay in the southeast Mediterranean.
A historical Egyptian named Muhammad Ali used wooden ships at this 1827 battle, at which Edward Codrington's British-led coalition broke the Ottoman Navy, forcing the recognition of Greek autonomy.

bonuses.leadin: Name these battles fought on or near the Mediterranean Sea, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this 1914 battle in which Max Hoffmann helped German forces defeat Russia near the site of a 1410 defeat by the Teutonic Knights. This battle was followed by the First Battle of the Masurian (maa-SOOR-ee-un) Lakes.

Along with his chief of staff Erich Ludendorff, this general rose to prominence after leading German forces at the Battle of Tannenberg. This general later served as president during the final years of the Weimar Republic.
acceptableAnswers: Paul Ludwig Hans Anton von Beneckendorff und von Hindenburg

parts.text: Hindenburg's victory at the Battle of Tannenberg came in the early stages of this 1914 to 1918 war.

bonuses.leadin: Alexander Samsonov committed suicide after this battle. For 10 points each:

parts.text: To control trade of these goods via the Indian Ocean, Hadim Suleiman Pasha expanded Ottoman control over all entrances to the Red Sea and Persian Gulf except Hormuz. Examples of these goods include clove and nutmeg.

The Ottomans vied for control of ports like Basra with this other empire, which they defeated at the Battle of Chaldiran. This empire's ruler Abbas I reconquered Caucasus territories with Janissary-inspired ghulam infantry.

Suleiman the Magnificent forged Ottoman cannons for this sultanate in modern-day Indonesia, which conquered the Sultanates of Aru and Johor. This sultanate's "pepper rajas" produced more than half of the world's pepper.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Ottoman operations in the Indian Ocean, for 10 points each.

parts.text: This model is used to describe the shapes of molecules based on electrostatic repulsion. In this theory, carbon dioxide, with two bonds and no lone pairs, is linear, while water, with one lone pair, is bent.
acceptableAnswers: do not accept Valence Bond Theory
The Valence shell electron pair repulsion

parts.text: This number is the of number electron pairs surrounding an atom. To derive it, one adds the number of bonds to the number of lone pairs.
This molecular arrangement, with bond angles of 109.5 degrees, is frequent through the first half of the periodic table, and molecules with this structure tend to be chiral. Methane is an example.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about molecular bonding, for 10 points each:
